A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same LROD/LR-YOLO study. The main text, Appendices A–G, checklist, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection benchmarks, ablations and generalization experiments in Section 5, plus per-class, restoration and qualitative results in Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same shared-backbone restoration architecture, detection and restoration losses, and parameter-gradient regularization.

E1.justification: Both use the same synthetic VOC/COCO haze and low-light datasets, RTTS, ExDark, and motion-blur, rain, snow and haze–rain scenarios. Detection and restoration task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership and training variants are identical within corresponding experiments, including restoration cascades, IA, GDIP, FeatEnHancer, and the SNR/PGD regularization comparisons.

E3.justification: The data splits, degradation synthesis ranges, evaluation metrics, detector configurations and training/testing procedures in Section 5 and the appendices are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4–7 retain the same component, alternative-regularization, backbone-sharing and coefficient ablations. Feature stability, degradation robustness and appendix qualitative analyses also match.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including Figure 2's Jacobian-norm distributions and checklist item 7's statement that error bars are not reported. No seed, repeated-run or significance information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains LR-YOLOv8's 53.2 mAP on RTTS and 54.5 mAP on ExDark.

T1.justification: The Lipschitz definitions, assumptions and mathematical remarks in Sections 3–4, together with the proof of Remark 3 in Appendix A, are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same functional-mismatch diagnosis, LROD contribution, and claims concerning detection stability, optimization smoothness and accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations of cascade instability and regularization effects are unchanged, as are Section 6's limitations and future directions and Appendix G's broader-impact discussion.

D1.justification: Architecture and dataset details, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosures and code/access statements are unchanged. The code-link destination also matches.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 37 reference entries and the paper's positioning relative to earlier research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first page changes the final author's displayed name from 'Lin Liang' to 'Liang Lin' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv sidebar moves downward. Figures 1–9, Tables 1–14, their captions and placement are unchanged; pages 2–26 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 makes a small author-name adjustment and updates/repositions the arXiv stamp. The scientific argument, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and appendices are unchanged, so these editorial adjustments produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
